QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_50

question.text: The SSE's 'minimum reporting standard' requires social enterprises to report on which sections per Chapter 2?

answer.text: Only financial statements in Ind-AS format.
Only beneficiary photographs and video testimonials.
General information, governance, funding, legal and statutory filings/reports, and aspects on stated intent + nature of impact + impact created.
Only monthly Form GST-3B filings and TDS returns.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 2.1, 'The minimum reporting standard includes various sections such as general information, governance, funding, legal and statutory filings/reports etc.' Entities must commit to this, requiring social enterprises to state an intent to create positive social impact, describe its nature, and report what impact they have created. It is this standardisation of reporting that 'selects in only those entities that are creating measurable positive social impact'. **The Trap:** Options A, B and D each narrow the reporting to a single stream, missing the holistic standard. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C (Compliance) treat LODR Chapter IXA/IXB disclosures — closely aligned to the minimum reporting standard. XV (RA) uses the same disclosures for impact-FPSE valuation. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When preparing the Annual Impact Report assurance, map each of the five reporting sections (general / governance / funding / legal-statutory / intent+nature+impact) to specific SAS assurance procedures — any section without assigned procedures creates an assurance gap that SEBI inspections readily identify.
